extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students studying functional analysis / operator theory
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of textbook problems in functional analysis (operators on Hilbert/Banach spaces, PDE maximum principles, variational methods, Sturm–Liouville theory, etc.) asking the reader to prove operator-theoretic and PDE facts, construct examples, and verify inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator norm bounded by Hilbert–Schmidt norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that ||T|| ≤ ||T||_{HS} for all T ∈ HS(E,F).

rubrics_metrics.name: HS(E,F) is Banach and Hilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that HS(E,F) equipped with the norm ||·||_{HS} is a Banach space. Show that in fact it is a Hilbert space.

rubrics_metrics.name: HS subset of compact operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that HS(E,F) ⊂ K(E,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Given x ∈ E, write x = Σ_{k=1}^∞ x_k e_k and set T_n(x) = Σ_{k=1}^n x_k T(e_k). Show that ||T_n - T|| → 0 as n → ∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-rank operators are Hilbert–Schmidt
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that any finite-rank operator from E into F belongs to HS(E,F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint preserves HS class and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T ∈ L(E,F). Prove that T ∈ HS(E,F) iff T^* ∈ HS(F,E) and that ||T^*||_{HS(F,E)} = ||T||_{HS(E,F)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-adjoint compact operator HS characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T ∈ K(E,E) with T^* = T, and let (λ_k) denote the sequence of eigenvalues of T. Show that T ∈ HS(E,E) iff Σ_{k=1}^∞ λ_k^2 < ∞ and that ||T||_{HS}^2 = Σ_{k=1}^∞ λ_k^2. Construct an example of an operator T ∈ K(E,E) with E = ℓ^2 such that T ∉ HS(E,E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition with HS gives HS
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G be another separable Hilbert space. Let T1 ∈ L(E,F) and T2 ∈ L(F,G). Show that T2 ◦ T1 ∈ HS(E,G) if either T1 or T2 belongs to HS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse of I+T for HS perturbation
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T ∈ HS(E,E) and assume N(I + T) = {0}. Show that (I + T) is bijective and that (I + T)^{-1} = I + S with S ∈ HS(E,E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthonormal basis of HS(E,F) by rank-one maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (e_k) (resp. (f_k)) be an orthonormal basis of E (resp. F). Consider the operator T_{k,l}: E → F defined by T_{k,l}(x) = (x, e_k) f_l. Show that (T_{k,l}) is an orthonormal basis of HS(E,F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral operator boundedness via kernel L2-norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Ω be an open subset of R^N, E = F = L^2(Ω). Let K ∈ L^2(Ω × Ω) and define (T u)(x) = ∫_Ω K(x,y) u(y) dy. Show that T ∈ L(E,E) and that ||T||_{L(E,E)} ≤ ||K||_{L^2(Ω×Ω)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral operator is Hilbert–Schmidt
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that T ∈ HS(E,E) and that ||T||_{HS(E,E)} ≤ ||K||_{L^2(Ω×Ω)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Let (e_j) be an orthonormal basis of L^2(Ω). Check that {e_j ⊗ e_k} is an orthonormal basis of L^2(Ω×Ω) and compute ||T(e_k)||_{L^2(Ω)}^2 = Σ_j |(T e_k, e_j)|^2 = Σ_j |(K, e_j ⊗ e_k)|^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel representation for HS operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversely, let T ∈ HS(E,E). Prove that there exists a unique function K ∈ L^2(Ω×Ω) such that (T u)(x)=∫ K(x,y)u(y) dy. K is called the kernel of T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Let t_{j,k} = (T e_k, e_j) and check that Σ_{j,k} |t_{j,k}|^2 < ∞. Define K = Σ_{j,k} t_{j,k} e_j ⊗ e_k and prove the integral representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Volterra operator is HS and compute HS norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume Ω=(0,1), E=L^2(Ω) and consider (T u)(x) = ∫_0^x u(t) dt. Show that T ∈ HS(E,E) and compute ||T||_{HS}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krein–Rutman: Int P disjoint from -P
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P ⊂ E be a closed convex cone with Int P ≠ ∅ and P ≠ E. Show that (Int P) ∩ (−P) = ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Exercise 1.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of α with ||x+u|| ≥ α for cone elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix u ∈ Int P. Show there exists α > 0 such that ||x + u|| ≥ α for all x ∈ P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Argue by contradiction and deduce −u ∈ P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of r with T u − r u ∈ P
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that there exists r > 0 such that T u − r u ∈ P (for fixed u ∈ Int P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvalue lower bound via cone order
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume some x ∈ P satisfies T(x + u) = λ x for some λ ∈ R. Prove that λ ≥ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Introduce order y ≥ z iff y − z ∈ P and use induction to show x ≥ u, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness and fixed-point to get positive eigenvector
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider F(x) = T((x+u)/||x+u||) for x ∈ P. Show F: P→P is continuous and F(P) ⊂ K for some compact K ⊂ E. Deduce existence of x1 ∈ P s.t. T(x1 + u) = λ1 x1 with λ1 = ||x1 + u|| ≥ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Apply Schauder fixed-point theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbed eigenvalue approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that for every ε > 0 there exists x_ε ∈ P such that T(x_ε + εu) = λ_ε x_ε with λ_ε = ||x_ε + εu|| ≥ r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of positive eigenvector
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove there exist x0 ∈ Int P and μ0 > 0 such that T x0 = μ0 x0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Show (x_ε) is bounded and extract limit as ε→0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of τ(a,b) for cone geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a ∈ Int P and b ∈ E, b ∉ P, prove existence of unique σ ∈ (0,1) so that (1−t)a+tb ∈ Int P for t∈[0,σ), (1−σ)a+σ b ∈ P, and (1−t)a+tb ∉ P for t∈(σ,1]. Set τ(a,b)=σ/(1−σ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness (up to scalar) of positive eigenvector in cone
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x ∈ P\{0} with T x = μ x. Prove μ = μ0 and x = m x0 for some m > 0, where μ0 and x0 are from previous construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Assume contrary, derive μ>0, x ∈ Int P and −x ∉ P; set y = x0 − τ0 x with τ0 = τ(x0, −x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral gap: other eigenvalues small
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x ∈ E\\{0} satisfy T x = μ x. Prove that either μ = μ0 and x = m x0 (m ≠0), or |μ| < μ0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Reduce to cases x ∉ P and −x ∉ P and use τ arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric multiplicity one for principal eigenvalue
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce N(T − μ0 I) = R x0, i.e., geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue μ0 is one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic multiplicity one for principal eigenvalue
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove N((T − μ0 I)^k) = R x0 for all k ≥ 2; algebraic multiplicity also one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Problem 36 to reduce to showing N((T − μ0 I)^2) = R x0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lomonosov: construct ball C avoiding origin under T
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix x0 with T x0 ≠ 0 and choose r ≤ ||T x0||/(2||T||) ≤ ||x0||/2, set C = {x: ||x − x0|| ≤ r}. Check 0 ∉ C and derive lower bound for ||T x|| on C so 0 ∉ T(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation by polynomials in T to approach x0
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that for every y ∈ E, y ≠ 0, there exists S ∈ A = span{I,T,T^2,...} (denoted Sy) such that ||S y − x0|| ≤ r/2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use assumption Ay = E for nontrivial Ay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local uniform approximation near any nonzero y
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that for every y ≠ 0 there exists ε_y > 0 (depending on y) such that ||S z − x0|| ≤ r for all z ∈ B(y, ε_y), where S is as in previous step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build continuous partition-of-unity-like q and positive lower bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite covering of T(C) by balls B(y_j, 1/2 ε_{y_j}), define q_j(x) = max{0, ε_{y_j} − ||T x − y_j||}, q(x)=Σ_j q_j(x). Check q continuous and q(x) ≥ min_j (1/2 ε_{y_j}) >0 for all x ∈ C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define continuous F mapping C into C near x0
rubrics_metrics.description: Set F(x) = (1/q(x)) Σ_j q_j(x) S_{y_j}(T x), x ∈ C. Prove F is continuous C→E and ||F(x) − x0|| ≤ r for all x ∈ C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use previous local approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness of F(C) and fixed point existence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove F(C) ⊂ K where K is compact subset of C. Deduce existence of ξ ∈ C with F(ξ) = ξ by Schauder fixed-point theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct finite-rank U and finite-dimensional invariant subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Set U = (1/q(ξ)) Σ_j q_j(ξ) (S_{y_j} ◦ T), with ξ fixed point; show U ∈ K(E), deduce Z = N(I − U) finite-dimensional and ξ ∈ Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show T preserves Z and conclude invariant subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Show T(Z) ⊂ Z and conclude existence of nontrivial closed invariant subspace for T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Show U ∈ A and deduce T ◦ U = U ◦ T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: operator on R^2 with only trivial invariant subspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a linear operator T: R^2 → R^2 that has no invariant subspaces except the trivial ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutant version: operator commuting with compact T has invariant subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T ∈ K(E), T ≠ 0, and R ∈ L(E) with R ◦ T = T ◦ R. Prove R admits a nontrivial closed invariant subspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Replace A by B = span{I, R, R^2, ...} and repeat previous steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal operator equivalent norm condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T ∈ L(H) be normal (T T^* = T^* T). Prove T is normal iff ||T u|| = ||T^* u|| for all u ∈ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Compute ||T(u+v)||^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonality of eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume u ∈ N(T − λ I) and v ∈ N(T − μ I) with λ ≠ μ. Show (u,v) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use that N(T^* − μ I) = N(T − μ I) and compute (T u, v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranges and nullspaces relations for normal operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove R(T) = R(T^*) = N(T)⊥ = N(T^*)⊥.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of range under adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f ∈ R(T). Check there exists u ∈ R(T^*) satisfying f = T u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Note H = R(T) ⊕ N(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit closure of ranges under T and T^*
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider a sequence u_n ∈ R(T^*) with u_n → u. Write u_n = T^* y_n and show T y_n converges to z with T^* z = f, establishing closure properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use question 1 and Cauchy sequence argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of ranges R(T)=R(T^*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that R(T) = R(T^*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm multiplicativity for normal operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that ||T^2|| = ||T||^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use inequality |T u|^2 ≤ |T^* T u| |u| = |T^2 u| |u|.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power norm equality for normal operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce ||T^p|| = ||T||^p for every integer p ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Consider even powers and extend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullspace stability under powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove N(T^2) = N(T) and deduce N(T^p) = N(T) for every integer p ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: If T^2 u = 0 then T u ∈ N(T) ∩ R(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isometry norm equals one
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is an isometry. Check that ||T|| = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of isometries via adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that T ∈ L(H) is an isometry iff T^* ◦ T = I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for unitary/isometry adjoint properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is an isometry. Prove equivalence of (a) T unitary, (b) T^* injective, (c) T ◦ T^* = I, (d) T^* is an isometry, (e) T^* is unitary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of non-unitary isometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an example of an isometry that is not a unitary operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Exercise 6.18 (shift on ℓ^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Range closedness and projection identity for isometries
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is an isometry. Prove R(T) is closed and T ◦ T^* = P_{R(T)}, the orthogonal projection on R(T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum dichotomy for isometries
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T is an isometry. Prove either T is unitary and σ(T) ⊂ {−1,+1}, or T is not unitary and σ(T) = [−1, +1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact isometries are finite-dimensional
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T ∈ K(H) is an isometry. Show that dim H < ∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skew-adjoint characterization via sesquilinear form
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove T ∈ L(H) is skew-adjoint iff (T u, u) = 0 for all u ∈ H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum of skew-adjoint operator
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T ∈ L(H) is skew-adjoint. Show that σ(T) ⊂ {0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Lax–Milgram (note: original statement as given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cayley transform yields unitary
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T ∈ L(H) is skew-adjoint. Set U = (T + I) ◦ (T − I)^{-1}. Check U well-defined, U = (T − I)^{-1} ◦ (T + I), U ◦ T = T ◦ U, and prove U is unitary (the Cayley transform).

rubrics_metrics.name: Converse: isometry Cayley implies skew-adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversely, let T ∈ L(H) be such that 1 ∉ σ(T). Assume U = (T + I)(T − I)^{-1} is an isometry. Prove T is skew-adjoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (1) for polar decomposition examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Property (1): there exists an isometry J from N(T) into N(T^*). Check assumption (1) is satisfied in these cases: (i) T injective, (ii) dim H < ∞, (iii) T normal, (iv) T = I − K with K ∈ K(H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example where property (1) fails
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an example in which property (1) (existence of isometry from N(T) into N(T^*)) is not satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Exercise 6.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar decomposition: relation P^2 = T^* T
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume we have a polar decomposition T = U ◦ P. Prove that P^2 = T^* ◦ T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of P on H
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that P is uniquely determined on H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Problem 39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of U on N(T)⊥
rubrics_metrics.description: Let T = U ◦ P be polar decomposition. Show U is uniquely determined on N(T)⊥.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar decomposition implies property (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume T admits a polar decomposition. Show that property (1) holds (i.e., existence of isometry J from N(T) into N(T^*)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Set J = U|_{N(T)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of polar decomposition under property (1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove every operator T ∈ L(H) satisfying property (1) admits a polar decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stronger property (2) gives unitary in polar decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume stronger assumption (2): there exists an isometry J from N(T) onto N(T^*). Show that T admits a polar decomposition T = U ◦ P where U is unitary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal operators admit commuting polar decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that every normal T ∈ L(H) admits a polar decomposition T = U ◦ P where U is unitary and U ◦ P = P ◦ U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization as P ◦ U under (2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show every operator T satisfying (2) can be factored as T = P ◦ U where U is unitary and P self-adjoint nonnegative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Apply previous to T^*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar decomposition for compact operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Show every operator T ∈ K(H) satisfying (1) admits a polar decomposition T = U ◦ P where P ∈ K(H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singular value decomposition for compact operator on separable H
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume H separable and T ∈ K(H). Prove there exist orthonormal bases (e_n) and (f_n) and nonnegative sequence (α_n) with α_n → 0 such that T u = Σ_n α_n (u, e_n) f_n for all u. Compute T^* and conversely show operators of this form are compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle: sign for test functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume ψ ∈ H^1 satisfies a(ψ, v) ≤ 0 for all v ∈ H^1_0(0,1) with v ≥ 0, and ψ(0) ≤ 0, ψ(1) ≤ 0. Prove ψ ≤ 0 on (0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Take v = (ψ+)+ in the inequality and use Exercise 8.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness and positivity of solution of homogeneous boundary value problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider - (p ζ')' + q ζ = 0, ζ(0) = 0, ζ(1) = 1. Show this has unique solution ζ and ζ ≥ 0 on (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonnegativity of solution u and boundary derivative signs
rubrics_metrics.description: From PDE - (p u')' + q u = f with f ≥ 0, f ≠ 0, show u ≥ 0 on (0,1) and deduce u'(0) ≥ 0 and u'(1) ≤ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary derivative formula via test function
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the identity p(1)|u'(1)| = ∫_0^1 f ζ where ζ solves the homogeneous problem above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Multiply equations appropriately and integrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersolution ϕ satisfies inequality for large B
rubrics_metrics.description: Set ϕ(x)= (e^{B x} −1)/(e^B −1). Check that for B sufficiently large depending on p and q, −(p ϕ')' + q ϕ ≤ 0 on (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower bound of ζ by scaled ϕ
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A = (e^B − 1)^{-1}. Prove ζ ≥ A ϕ on (0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Apply maximum principle to ψ = Aϕ − ζ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict negativity of boundary derivative u'(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce u'(1) < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use earlier boundary derivative formula with positivity of ζ and f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict positivity of u'(0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check u'(0) > 0 (by symmetry/change of variable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower bounds in interior via barrier v
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose δ small and γ as specified; let v solve - (p v')' + q v = 0 on (δ,1−δ) with v(δ)=v(1−δ)=γ. Show u ≥ v ≥ 0 on (δ,1−δ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivity of v inside
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove v > 0 on (δ,1−δ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: If v(x0)=0 for some interior x0, apply uniqueness (Cauchy–Lipschitz–Picard) contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong maximum principle conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce u(x) > 0 for all x ∈ (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative lower bound by x(1−x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove there is a constant a > 0 depending only on p and q such that u(x) ≥ a x (1 − x) ∫_0^1 f(t) t (1 − t) dt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: start with p ≡ 1 and q constant, then reduce general case via change of variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsolution/supersolution first monotone iterate inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Given subsolution v and supersolution w for −u'' + u = h(u) with 0 ≤ v ≤ w, show v ≤ u1 ≤ w for the first iterate u1 solving −u1'' + u1 = h(v) with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Apply maximum principle to u1 − w and u1 − v.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone iteration: monotonicity and lower bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove by induction v ≤ u_n and u_{n+1} ≤ u_n for all n ≥ 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergence in L^2 and nonlinear term convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce the sequence (u_n) converges in L^2(I) to a limit u and that h(u_n) → h(u) in L^2(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak formulation and membership in H^1_0
rubrics_metrics.description: Show u ∈ H^1_0(I) and that ∫ u' φ' + ∫ u φ = ∫ h(u) φ for all φ ∈ H^1_0(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity to classical solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude u ∈ C^2([0,1]) and is a classical solution of the boundary value problem −u'' + u = h(u), u(0)=u(1)=0 with v ≤ u ≤ w.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence for power nonlinearity using small subsolution
rubrics_metrics.description: For h(t) = t^α (0 < α < 1), let v(x)=ε sin(πx), w≡1. Show for ε small the assumptions hold and deduce existence of solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle gives ũ ≤ 1 for any solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Show any other solution ũ ∈ C^2([0,1]) of −u'' + u = u^α satisfies ũ ≤ 1 on I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider point where ũ achieves max.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone iteration from 1 yields ũ ≤ u
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the monotone sequence starting from u0 ≡ 1 satisfies u_{n+1} ≤ u_n and deduce any other solution ũ ≤ u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral identity to compare solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Show ũ ≤ u_n and deduce ∫ (ũ^α u − u^α ũ) = 0 leading to equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude that ũ = u on I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use monotonicity of t ↦ t^{α−1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variational lower bound for functional F
rubrics_metrics.description: Define F(u) = (1/2)∫ (u'^2 + u^2) − ∫ g(u) with g(t)= (1/(α+1))(t_+)^{α+1}. Prove there exists C such that F(u) ≥ (1/2) ||u||_{H^1}^2 − C ||u||_{H^1}^{α+1} for all u ∈ H^1_0(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of minimizer for F and m>−∞
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce m = inf_{v ∈ H^1_0} F(v) > −∞ and that the infimum is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use boundedness of minimizing sequence in H^1 and weak convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative minimizer values exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that m < 0 by testing F(ε v) < 0 for small ε and suitable v ∈ H^1_0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convexity inequality for g
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that g(b) − g(a) ≥ (a_+)^α (b − a) for all a, b ∈ R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler–Lagrange for minimizer yields weak equation
rubrics_metrics.description: Let u be minimizer of F on H^1_0. Prove ∫ u' v' + ∫ u v = ∫ (u_+)^α v for all v ∈ H^1_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: consider F(u) ≤ F(u + t v) and let t → 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity and positivity of variational solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce u ∈ C^2([0,1]) is solution of −u'' + u = (u_+)^α with u ≥ 0 and u ≠ 0, hence u > 0 by strong maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré–Wirtinger L∞ vs L1 inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove ||u − ū||_{L∞(I)} ≤ ||u'||_{L1(I)} for all u ∈ W^{1,1}(I), where ū = ∫ u.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use that u(x0)=ū for some x0 ∈ [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimality of constant in L∞–L1 inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the constant 1 in previous inequality is optimal: sup over functions with ||u'||_{L1}=1 of ||u − ū||_{L∞} equals 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: construct sequence of smooth functions concentrating near one endpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonattainment of sup in previous inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the sup in the optimality statement is not achieved (no function attains it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré inequality for W^{1,1}_0 with best constant 1/2
rubrics_metrics.description: Show ||u||_{L∞(I)} ≤ (1/2) ||u'||_{L1(I)} for all u ∈ W^{1,1}_0(I) and that 1/2 is best constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use pointwise estimates |u(x) − u(0)| ≤ ∫_0^x |u'| and symmetrize.

rubrics_metrics.name: General embedding inequalities for W^{1,p}
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce inequalities ||u − ū||_{L^q} ≤ C ||u'||_{L^p} for u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) and ||u||_{L^q} ≤ C ||u'||_{L^p} for u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I), for 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞ and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞; best constants achieved when 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞ and 1 < p ≤ ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: minimize ||u'||_{L^p} under constraints on the L^q norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variational formulation for best constant in L2 case
rubrics_metrics.description: To find best constant in ||u − ū||_{L2} ≤ C ||u'||_{L2} for u ∈ H^1(I), define H = {f ∈ L^2: ∫ f = 0} and consider operator T mapping f to u solving weak problem; use eigenvalues to compute best constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenvalue relation gives best constant
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that best constant C = √λ_1 where λ_1 is largest eigenvalue of associated compact self-adjoint operator; compute λ_1 explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Rayleigh quotient and compactness of T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted L1 Poincaré inequality
Optimality of 1/2 in L1 inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Show sup{ ||u − ū||_{L1} ; ||u'||_{L1} = 1 } = 1/2 and discuss whether supremum is attained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convex variational problem with singular boundary behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Let j be convex with j(0)=0 and singular behavior at ±1; define ϕ on H^1_0 by integral involving j and f. Check ϕ convex lower-semicontinuous and show existence of unique minimizer u with ||u||_∞ < 1 for f ∈ L^∞, and derive Euler–Lagrange equation −u'' + j'(u) = f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truncation and approximation for existence in less regular f
rubrics_metrics.description: For f ∈ L^2, let f_n be truncations and u_n corresponding solutions; prove uniform bounds j'(u_n) in L^2, H^2 bounds, and convergence to u satisfying the PDE with ||u||_∞ < 1 under extra growth conditions on j'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: multiply equation by j'(u_n), apply Fatou and truncation/compactness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sturm–Liouville operator: compact self-adjoint inverse
rubrics_metrics.description: With Au = −(p u')' + q u on (0,1) Dirichlet, define coercive form ã and associated operator T: H → H (with H = H^1_0 endowed with ã). Show T is self-adjoint and compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: identity embedding H→L^2 compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of eigenvalues of T and A
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (λ_k) be eigenvalues of A and (μ_k) eigenvalues of T. Show μ_k > 0 and λ_k = 1/μ_k − M, and T(e_k) = μ_k e_k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rayleigh quotient representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove (T w, w)_H = ∫_0^1 w^2 and the Rayleigh quotient R(w) = (T w, w)_H / ||w||_H^2 = (∫ w^2) / ||w||_H^2 relates to a(w,w)/∫ w^2 + M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Problem 37 for relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variational characterization of eigenvalues (min formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove λ_k = min{ a(w,w)/∫ w^2 ; w ⟂ e_j for j=1,...,k−1 }, and analogous min-max/ max-min characterizations over k-dimensional subspaces and codimension (k−1) subspaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: apply variational principle (Rayleigh–Ritz).

rubrics_metrics.name: Neumann boundary case analogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove similar min-max variational characterizations for the Sturm–Liouville operator with Neumann boundary conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivity and simplicity of first eigenfunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Let w_0 minimizer normalized to ∫ w_0^2 =1. Show A w_0 = λ_1 w_0, set w_1 = |w_0|, prove w_1 is minimizer, Aw_1 = λ_1 w_1, w_1 > 0 on (0,1) and boundary derivative signs. Show any eigenfunction for λ_1 is a scalar multiple of w_1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use Exercise 8.11, strong maximum principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: nonnegative normalized eigenfunction equals principal one
rubrics_metrics.description: Show any ψ ∈ H^1_0 with Aψ = μ ψ, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ ψ^2 = 1 must coincide with w_1 and hence μ = λ_1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy minimizer for quartic nonlinearity and existence of two minimizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a(v,v) + (1/4) ∫ |v|^4 have negative infimum m < 0. Prove inf is achieved by u_0 ∈ H^1_0 which solves −u'' + q u + u^3 = 0; show |u_0| also minimizer and eventually there are exactly two minimizers ±U_0 with U_0 > 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivity alternative for minimizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that any minimizer u_0 of the quartic problem is either strictly positive on (0,1) or strictly negative on (0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of nontrivial nonnegative solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U_1 be solution ≥ 0; define ρ_1 = U_1^2 and functional J(ρ). Prove strict convexity inequality (J(ρ) − J(ρ_1) ≥ (1/2) ∫ (ρ − ρ_1)^2) for ρ in K, leading to uniqueness of nontrivial nonnegative solution U_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use integration by parts and identity relating u and U_1 to ρ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonic oscillator function space V separability
rubrics_metrics.description: Let p ∈ C(R), p ≥ 0. Define V = {v ∈ H^1(R); ∫ p v^2 < ∞} with scalar product (u,v)_V = ∫ (u' v' + u v + p u v). Check V is a separable Hilbert space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of C∞_c in V
rubrics_metrics.description: Show C^∞_c(R) is dense in V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use cut-off functions and convolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coercivity of form and solvability on R
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming p(x) ≥ δ > 0 for |x| ≥ A, prove a(u,v) = ∫ (u' v' + p u v) is coercive on V and hence for every f ∈ L^2(R) there is a unique u ∈ V solving a(u,v) = ∫ f v for all v ∈ V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity and decay for solutions on R
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming f ∈ L^2 ∩ C(R), show solution u ∈ C^2(R) with −u'' + p u = f and u(x) → 0 as |x| → ∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversely: classical solutions lie in V
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove any classical solution u of −u'' + p u = f with decay at infinity belongs to V and satisfies the weak formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: multiply by cutoff ζ_n^2 u and use coercivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness of resolvent under p→∞ at infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume lim_{|x|→∞} p(x) = +∞. Then for f ∈ L^2 set u = T f solving weak problem; prove T: L^2 → L^2 is self-adjoint and compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use compact embedding V ↪ L^2 from Corollary 4.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral decomposition and eigenfunctions for harmonic oscillator
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce existence of sequence λ_n → ∞ and Hilbert basis (e_n) of L^2(R) with e_n ∈ V ∩ C^2 and −e_n'' + p e_n = λ_n e_n on R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermite polynomial eigenfunctions for p(x)=x^2
rubrics_metrics.description: For p(x) = x^2, check that eigenfunctions are of form e_n(x) = e^{−x^2/2} P_n(x) with eigenvalues λ_n = 2 n + 1 and P_n polynomials of degree n.
